title: Hom from the degree-zero structure sheaf is zeroth hypercohomology
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $D(\mathcal O_X)$ its unbounded derived category [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $\Gamma(X,-)$ be the module-valued global-sections functor [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and let $F(E)$ be the underlying additive group of $H^0(R\Gamma(X,E))$, with unbounded derived global sections as in [def-pc-global-derived-rhom]. For every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ there is an additive bijection $e_E:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(\mathcal O_X[0],E)\simeq F(E)$, natural in $E$: for $f:E\to E\prime$ and $g:\mathcal O_X[0]\to E$, $e_{E\prime}(f\circ g)=F(f)(e_E(g))$. No quasi-coherence, boundedness, quasi-compactness, or separatedness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Choose a K-injective representative J of E using [lem-pc-scheme-modules-grothendieck-abelian] and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The K-injective localization bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies derived maps from the degree-zero structure sheaf with homotopy classes of chain maps into J.

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph; structure-sheaf case

proof.text: Evaluation at 1 identifies O_X-linear maps O_X → J^n with global sections of J^n. Chain-map equations from O_X[0] say the section in degree zero is closed. A homotopy from this one-term source is a section in degree -1 whose differential is the difference of the two cycles. Hence homotopy classes are the additive group H^0(Γ(X,J)). The K-injective resolution computation in [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] identifies this group with H^0(RΓ(X,E)).

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph; structure-sheaf case

proof.text: For a derived morphism f between K-injective representatives, the localization bijection supplies a chain-map lift. Postcomposition on cycles is application of Γ(f), so it induces exactly F(f) on H^0. Changing the lift by a homotopy leaves its map on cohomology unchanged. The K-injective comparison maps intertwine the same operations; consequently the additive equivalences descend independently of representatives and obey the stated naturality equation.

theorem derivedStructureSheaf_hom_hypercohomology (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)))
    let F := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) 0 ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) AddCommGrpCat
    ∃ e : ∀ E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))) ⟶ E) ≃+ F.obj E,
      ∀ (E E' : schemeDerivedCategory X) (f : E ⟶ E') (g :
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ⟶ E),
        e E' (g ≫ f) = F.map f (e E g)
